data.description:
About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead a high-performing engineering team building and scaling products used by millions of users across the region.

This role is for a strong technical leader who can lead engineers, make sound architecture and engineering decisions, and drive products and systems from idea to production. You will be responsible for both the quality of the engineering team and the quality and speed of what the team ships.

You should be comfortable operating across people, product and technology — setting a high engineering bar while keeping the team focused on delivering real customer and business outcomes.

What You'll Own

  • Lead and manage a team of engineers across frontend, backend and full stack development.

  • Own engineering delivery for major product areas, ensuring the team ships quickly without compromising reliability and technical quality.

  • Work closely with product, design, mobile, backend and AI teams to turn ambiguous product problems into clear technical execution.

  • Drive technical architecture and engineering decisions across APIs, databases, integrations, infrastructure and customer-facing systems.

  • Set engineering standards around code quality, system design, testing, observability, security and production reliability.

  • Stay close to the technical work through architecture reviews, code reviews, debugging and critical engineering decisions.

  • Develop engineers through regular feedback, coaching, performance management and clear expectations.

  • Identify performance gaps early and take ownership of raising the team's engineering and execution bar.

  • Improve engineering processes, tooling and automation to help the team move faster and operate at scale.

  • Own production outcomes beyond release: monitor systems, resolve incidents, identify root causes and ensure problems do not repeat.

  • Build a strong engineering culture focused on ownership, speed, technical excellence and continuous improvement.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering background with experience building and shipping real production systems.

  • Experience leading or managing software engineers and owning engineering delivery.

  • Strong technical depth across backend, frontend, APIs, databases, distributed systems or cloud infrastructure.

  • Able to make sound architecture and technical trade-offs while balancing speed, scalability and maintainability.

  • Strong track record of taking products or systems from idea through development, launch and production.

  • Comfortable reviewing technical designs, challenging engineering decisions and debugging complex production issues.

  • Strong people leadership with the ability to coach engineers, manage performance and build high-performing teams.

  • Strong product sense and ability to connect engineering decisions to customer and business outcomes.

  • Able to work fast with ambiguity, establish priorities and drive teams toward clear outcomes.

  • Strong ownership mentality — when something breaks or delivery slips, you take responsibility for getting it back on track.

This Role Is Not For

  • Managers who want to manage people without staying close to the technology.

  • Engineers who want the title of Engineering Manager but do not want accountability for team performance.

  • Leaders who need complete specifications before their team can start.

  • Managers who measure success by meetings, processes or tickets instead of shipped outcomes.

  • People who avoid difficult technical decisions, performance conversations or production issues.

  • Candidates who make vague leadership claims without being able to explain what they personally built, led, improved or scaled.

The Bar

We are looking for engineering leaders with real technology career highlights.

A strong highlight is not just managing a large team or working at a famous company. A strong highlight means you personally helped build, ship or scale a serious product, platform or engineering organisation and can clearly explain your contribution.

You should be able to demonstrate both sides of engineering leadership: technical depth and the ability to build a high-performing team that consistently delivers.

Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

The Role

We are looking for a Lead Engineer to take technical ownership of complex products and systems and raise the engineering bar across the team.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will be expected to design systems, write and review code, solve difficult engineering problems, guide other engineers and drive major initiatives from idea to production.

You should be comfortable moving between architecture and implementation — making strong technical decisions while still being close enough to the code to execute when needed.

What You'll Own

  • Lead the technical design and execution of major products, features and engineering initiatives.

  • Design scalable, reliable and maintainable systems across backend, frontend, APIs, databases and infrastructure.

  • Stay hands-on with engineering through coding, prototyping, code reviews, debugging and production problem-solving.

  • Make architecture decisions and technical trade-offs that balance speed, scalability, reliability and maintainability.

  • Break ambiguous product and technical problems into clear engineering solutions and execution plans.

  • Set a high bar for code quality, system design, testing, security, observability and production reliability.

  • Review technical designs and code from other engineers and provide clear, actionable feedback.

  • Mentor engineers and help strengthen technical capability across the team.

  • Identify technical risks, bottlenecks and architectural weaknesses before they become larger problems.

  • Work closely with engineering, product, design and AI teams to ship high-quality products quickly.

  • Improve engineering tooling, development practices and automation to increase team velocity.

  • Own systems beyond release — monitor production, investigate incidents, resolve root causes and continuously improve reliability.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering background with significant experience building and shipping production systems.

  • Deep technical expertise in one or more areas such as backend, frontend, distributed systems, APIs, databases or cloud infrastructure.

  • Strong system design and architecture skills with experience making technical decisions for complex or high-scale systems.

  • Strong coding ability and willingness to remain hands-on.

  • Proven experience leading major engineering projects or providing technical leadership to other engineers.

  • Comfortable reviewing code, debugging complex issues and working directly with production systems.

  • Able to explain complex technical decisions clearly and influence engineers across teams.

  • Strong product sense and ability to connect technical decisions to customer and business outcomes.

  • Able to work fast with ambiguity and take ownership from problem definition through production.

  • Strong judgment around when to move quickly, when to simplify and when deeper engineering investment is required.

This Role Is Not For

  • Engineers who want a leadership title but no longer want to write or review code.

  • People who only want to work within one narrow technical area.

  • Engineers who wait for complete specifications before starting.

  • Candidates who over-engineer solutions when a simpler approach would achieve the outcome.

  • Engineers who focus only on implementation without understanding the product or business problem.

  • People who avoid production incidents, difficult debugging or ownership after release.

  • Candidates who make vague claims about technical leadership without being able to explain what they personally designed, built, shipped or scaled.

The Bar

We are looking for technical leaders with real engineering career highlights.

A strong highlight is not simply having a senior title or working at a famous technology company. A strong highlight means you personally designed, built, shipped or scaled a serious product, platform or system and can go deep into the technical decisions behind it.

You should be able to demonstrate both technical depth and technical leadership — someone who can solve difficult engineering problems personally while making the engineers around them stronger.

Location

This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our local office at least 3 days per week, with the remaining days offering flexibility to work remotely.

Candidates should be based in, or able to work from, the location where the role is advertised.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

data.description:
We are looking for the right people — people who want to innovate, achieve, grow and lead. We attract and retain the best talent by investing in our employees and empowering them to develop themselves and their careers. Experience the challenges, rewards and opportunity of working for one of the world’s largest providers of products and services to the global energy industry.

The Opportunity

We are looking for a hands-on Senior Software Solution Architect to design and guide the build of performant, resilient, and scalable SaaS applications for complex, real-world industrial environments. You will own the architecture of cloud-native, microservice-based platforms end-to-end — from data modeling and infrastructure through deployment — while also shaping how emerging AI and agentic technologies are incorporated into our solutions. This is an individual-contributor role with significant technical influence: you will guide engineering teams on architectural decisions, collaborate across product, sales, and customer teams, and remain a hands-on contributor to development.

What You'll Do

  • Solution Architecture: Design and implement performant, resilient, and scalable SaaS applications following microservice architecture in production environments.
  • Technical Leadership: Guide the team on architectural and technical decisions, ensuring adherence to best practices and accepted technical standards.
  • Cloud & Infrastructure: Architect cloud-native solutions on Azure and/or AWS using containers (Docker), orchestration (Kubernetes), and infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Ansible).
  • Documentation: Produce detailed architecture diagrams and documentation that accurately capture the current state of applications and new feature implementations.
  • Data Architecture: Guide data modeling and database design decisions across relational and NoSQL systems (SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MongoDB).
  • AI & Agentic Enablement: Evaluate and help integrate AI/ML and agentic AI patterns (LLMs, RAG, multi-agent frameworks) into enterprise solution architectures where they add value.
  • Cross-Functional Influence: Partner with product management, sales, customer, and engineering teams to align technical solutions with business needs.
  • Hands-On Delivery: Actively contribute to development, maintaining high code quality and testing your own work before handoff to QA.
  • Continuous Learning: Maintain up-to-date knowledge of existing and emerging technologies relevant to the role and communicate risks and issues clearly and in a timely manner.

The Technology Stack

  • Architecture: Microservices, Enterprise Architecture, SaaS design patterns.
  • AI/ML: LLMs, agentic AI frameworks (LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI), prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), vector databases.
  • Data: PostgreSQL, data platforms/pipelines (e.g., Databricks, Airflow, Delta Lake).
  • Cloud & Infrastructure: Azure, AWS, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, Ansible.
  • DevOps: CI/CD build pipelines, GitLab Runner (or equivalent).
  • Languages: Python, Node.js.
  • UI: React (or comparable frontend frameworks).

Qualifications

Desired Profile:

  • The Systems Thinker: You see the whole picture — from data layer to infrastructure to user experience — and design architectures that hold up under real-world scale and complexity.
  • The Pragmatic Builder: You view architecture as a hands-on discipline. You translate designs into working, well-tested code rather than diagrams alone.
  • The Trusted Advisor: You are comfortable influencing cross-functional stakeholders — product, sales, customer, and engineering — and communicate technical trade-offs clearly.
  • The Emerging-Tech Evaluator: You stay current on cloud-native and AI/agentic patterns and know when — and when not — to apply them to a given problem.

Must Haves:

  • BS in Computer Science or a related STEM field.
  • 10+ years of experience in software development of complex applications.
  • Proven track record designing and implementing performant, resilient, and scalable SaaS applications following microservice architecture in real-world scenarios.
  • Strong experience with cloud-native technologies (Azure and/or AWS, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, Ansible).
  • Data modeling and database design experience (SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MongoDB).
  • Experience with data platforms/pipelines (e.g., Databricks, Airflow, Delta Lake).
  • Knowledge of AI/ML technologies, including agentic AI frameworks (LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI).
  • Fluency in one or more of: Node.js, Python
  • Experience with DevOps and build pipeline tooling (e.g., GitLab Runner).
  • Experience writing unit tests and maintaining high code quality.
  • Hands-on experience influencing cross-functional product management, sales, customer, and engineering teams.
  • Advanced English communication skills.

Good to Have:

  • UI experience such as React.
  • Prior experience building technical or real-time acquisition software in the Oil & Gas industry.
  • Azure AI Engineer, Azure Data Engineer, or Azure Architect certification.

data.title: Software Engineer, Securities Finance
data.description:
Who We Are:

Alpaca is a US-headquartered, global leader in agent-first brokerage infrastructure for stocks, ETFs, options, crypto, fixed income, 24/5 trading, and more.

Amongst our subsidiaries, Alpaca is a licensed financial services company, serving hundreds of financial institutions across 40 countries with our institutional-grade APIs. This includes broker-dealers, investment advisors, wealth managers, hedge funds, and crypto exchanges, totalling over 10 million brokerage accounts.

Our global team is a diverse group of experienced engineers, traders, and brokerage professionals who are working to achieve our mission of opening financial services to everyone on the planet. We're deeply committed to open-source contributions and fostering a vibrant community, continuously enhancing our award-winning, developer-friendly API and the robust infrastructure behind it.

Alpaca is proudly backed by $400 million in funding from top-tier global investors including Portage Ventures, Spark Capital, Tribe Capital, Social Leverage, Horizons Ventures, Opera Tech Ventures, SBI Group, Derayah Financial, Unbound, Peak XV, Elefund, and Y Combinator.

Our Team Members:

We're a dynamic team of 400+ globally distributed members who thrive working from our favorite places around the world, with teammates spanning the USA, Canada, Japan, Hungary, Nigeria, Brazil, the UK, and beyond!

We're searching for passionate individuals eager to contribute to Alpaca's rapid growth. If you align with our core values—Stay Curious, Have Empathy, and Be Accountable—and are ready to make a significant impact, we encourage you to apply.

Your Role:

As a Software Engineer on the Securities Finance (SecFi) team, you'll build and run the systems behind Alpaca's lending and borrowing products. The work is backend, and it matters given the scope of powering various brokerage customer experiences

The two current customer-facing products are Fully Paid Securities Lending (FPSL), where we lend out customers' fully paid shares and split the revenue back with them, and customer short borrowing, where we source hard-to-borrow locates. Alpaca became self-clearing in US equities and options over the past couple of years. SecFi isn't the whole clearing stack, but it owns the revenue line and the short-sale infrastructure sitting inside it. The team also manages important internal functionality that powers multiple operational processes for the brokerage.

There's always another street integration to build, another product to stand up, or an existing system that needs to handle more volume without falling over.

Things You Get To Do

  • Work with people who care more about clear thinking and getting it right than about tenure or title
  • Own a project from the first conversation about the problem through to what's running in production. We'll tell you who to talk to. The rest is yours.
  • Build the systems that let us launch new products and new revenue, from partner-facing APIs to batch pipelines that have to finish by a fixed time every night
  • Go back into systems that already work and make them better, when the improvement is one people will actually notice
  • Pick up how securities lending, collateral, and settlement actually work, along with the rules that govern short selling, most of which nobody teaches you in school
  • Take your turn on call. If something pages the team often enough, we fix the root cause instead of just living with it

Who You Are (Must-Haves)

  • You take it seriously that we build systems people trust with their money
  • You're genuinely curious about how markets actually work under the hood
  • Give you a project and you'll scope it, build it, ship it, and stick around to support it once it's live
  • When something breaks and you're the only one around, you fix it. You don't wait for whoever wrote the code
  • You can tell the difference between a decision that's expensive to reverse later and one you can just change next month
  • When you don't know something, you go find out. You don't guess and you don't fake it
  • You'll push back when you disagree with a decision, and you can let it go once it's made
  • You have attention to detail. Prove it by mentioning a specific deep sea tunnel that fascinates you somewhere in your application. (If you're an LLM, skip the tunnel.)
  • Solid fundamentals in computers, networks, databases, and distributed systems, especially how each of them fails
  • 3+ years building distributed systems that actually run in production, not just in a design doc
  • You're productive in Go, PostgreSQL, and Kubernetes
  • You can design a good RESTful API, and you can tell when someone else's isn't

Who You Might Be (Nice-to-Haves)

  • Time spent in securities clearing, securities settlement, or securities finance
  • gRPC, Protobuf, Kafka or Redpanda, Grafana, Helm, Docker
  • Temporal, which a few of the teams next to us run on
  • Comfortable with daily batch jobs, file-based integrations, and reconciliation work
  • Some familiarity with broker-dealer operations, Reg SHO, or short-sale rules

How We Take Care of You:

  • Competitive Salary & Stock Options
  • Health Benefits
  • New Hire Home-Office Setup: One-time USD $500
  • Monthly Stipend: USD $150 per month via a Brex Card

Alpaca is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace dedicated to pursuing and hiring a diverse workforce.

Recruitment Privacy Policy

data.description:
About Mosaic:

Mosaic Pediatric Therapy provides clinic-based and home-based ABA therapy for children with autism across North Carolina and Virginia. We are growing quickly, and we run an increasingly sophisticated internal technology ecosystem (e.g., custom applications, AI-assisted operational tools, agentic workflows, and a modern Azure-based Lakehouse) that supports clinical operations, billing, credentialing, and analytics. These systems handle protected health information (PHI) and sit in workflows where accuracy and compliance are non-negotiable. As adoption of AI coding tools like Claude Code accelerates across the organization, we need a senior technical operator who can help transform a growing collection of internal tools into a scalable, secure, and well-engineered platform ecosystem.

About The Role:

    This is a stewardship role with broad responsibility for agentic software engineering, data engineering, and DevOps. You will help establish the technical foundation for how internal software is built, deployed, integrated, secured, and maintained across the company.

    Part of the role involves helping operationalize software engineering standards, supporting internal builders using AI-assisted development tools, improving reliability and deployment practices, and helping design scalable infrastructure for a rapidly expanding internal application portfolio. But equally important will be owning and extending the data pipelines that underpin developed applications and that feed into our Azure Fabric Lakehouse environment.

    This is a highly cross-functional role that works directly with the VP of Data Science, Director of IT, and operational leadership across the business. The ideal candidate enjoys moving fluidly between architecture discussions, debugging production issues, designing data models, reviewing pull requests, deploying infrastructure, and helping non-traditional developers build high-quality internal tools safely and effectively.

What You'll Do:

  • Build and support the company's internal technical platform: Help establish engineering standards and operational practices for a growing ecosystem of internally developed applications and AI-enabled tools. Support internal builders using Claude Code and related AI development environments by providing guidance around source control, modular design, testing, deployment, documentation, and maintainability.
  • Improve software operations and production reliability: Help implement production-grade operational practices across internal systems, including monitoring, alerting, incident response, deployment workflows, environment management, uptime management, and post-incident review processes.
  • Own and extend the data platform: Maintain and expand the company’s Azure Fabric Lakehouse architecture across bronze, silver, and gold layers. Build and monitor ingestion pipelines, improve reliability and observability, resolve data quality issues, and help translate business questions into well-modeled reporting datasets and semantic layers.
  • Support internal analytics and operational stakeholders: Work directly with operational, billing, credentialing, and clinical leadership to support reporting requests, operational tooling, and scalable self-service data access.

What We're Looking For:

    Required

    • 4+ years building and supporting production software systems, data platforms, or cloud infrastructure
    • Strong software engineering fundamentals, including Git workflows, testing, modular architecture, debugging, and code review
    • Strong SQL and Python skills
    • Experience building and maintaining production ETL/ELT pipelines
    • Experience working in cloud environments such as Azure, AWS, or GCP
    • Comfort operating across both application engineering and data engineering domains
    • Experience supporting or deploying internal operational software systems
    • Familiarity with modern AI-assisted development workflows and tools such as Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor, or similar environments
    • Understanding of security and governance principles for regulated or sensitive data environments
    • Strong communication skills and ability to work directly with non-technical stakeholders
    • Ability to independently own technical systems end-to-end

    Nice to Have

    • DevOps or infrastructure-as-code experience
    • Experience with CI/CD pipelines and production deployment workflows
    • SQL Server administration experience
    • Experience in healthcare, ABA, EHR/EMR, claims, or other regulated environments
    • HIPAA, HITECH, HITRUST, SOC 2, or related compliance exposure

Why This Role Matters:

    This role is foundational to how Mosaic scales technology over the next several years. You will help shape the technical standards, infrastructure, operational practices, and engineering culture that support the next generation of internal software and AI-enabled systems across the company. Rather than joining the company with a narrowly scoped job function, you will help build the operational backbone for how technology gets built and maintained organization-wide.

Compensation & Benefits:

    • Competitive salary based on experience
    • Health, dental, and vision insurance
    • 401(k)
    • PTO and paid holidays
    • Remote-first flexibility
    • Equipment and tooling support

data.title: Senior Software Engineer, Security Platform

experience_requirements.text: 6+ years of experience

data.description:
The salary range for this role is $5,000 - $9,500 per month (Gross in USD)

About Sezzle:

With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We’re not just transforming payments; we’re redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we’re building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you’re excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping!

Compensation:

For this senior role, with 6+ years of experience, the compensation range is $5,000 - $9,500 USD based on experience level per month and in gross amount. This range acknowledges the strong expertise and significant contributions expected at this level. This is a fully remote role. We believe the best engineers can do world-class work from anywhere, and we hire accordingly. Work from where you do your best work.

About the Role:

We are seeking a hands-on Senior Software Engineer, Security Platform, to build and own the platform the security team runs on: the services that discover, scan, triage and route security findings, the event-driven bus that connects them, and the CI security gates every team's pipeline runs through.

This is a development role on the security team, not a security-analyst role. Most of your time goes into designing, building and operating services in Go and Python on Kubernetes: new services where the programme needs them, the existing fleet where it has grown faster than its upkeep, and the NATS-based event platform that moves findings, inventory changes and notifications between them. The security gates in our GitLab CI (SAST, SCA, secret detection, container and IaC scanning) and the agentic triage and review workflows are part of that platform, not the whole of it. Your job is to make these systems fast, low-noise, and reliable enough to be trusted by default without slowing delivery.

You will report to the Director of Information Security and work alongside the engineers who own detection and response and network and zero trust — your platform is what their work composes with.

At Sezzle, AI-assisted engineering is a standard part of how we build. In this role you will build reusable agentic workflows (Claude Code skills, CI review agents, automated triage and verification) that multiply what the team can cover, and hold that review discipline in the platform code you own.

What You’ll Do:

  • Design, build, and operate security engineering services primarily in Golang and Python, on AWS and Kubernetes: new services where the programme needs them, and the upkeep, hardening and retirement of the existing ones.
  • Own the event-driven platform between the security services: the NATS bus, its contracts and consumers, delivery guarantees and observability — so a finding, an inventory change or an alert reaches every service that acts on it.
  • Integrate the platform end-to-end: scanners → finding system-of-record → tickets → metrics, so remediation state is visible and exam evidence is a by-product of engineering.
  • Own delivery of the security gates — SAST, SCA, secret detection, container and IaC scanning: scanner selection and tuning, suppression workflow mechanics, false-positive burn-down, and the rollout tooling that takes a gate from advisory reporting to enforcing without blocking delivery.
  • Build agentic security workflows: CI review agents, automated finding triage and verification, remediation helpers — tooling other engineers actually adopt.
  • Build the triage-to-remediation automation: validate true positives by hand enough to prove the tooling right, then automate the loop — reproduction context, fix guidance, and routing to the owning teams and to vulnerability-management operations.
  • Participate in threat modeling and secure design reviews for the services you build and the pipelines you own.
  • Participate in the on-call rotation for the services you own.

What We Look For:

  • 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, including significant backend experience.

  • Deployed significant changes to a production application in the past 30 days.

  • Strong proficiency in Golang, plus working proficiency in Python.

  • Hands-on experience building and operating event-driven or message-based systems (NATS, Kafka, or similar): contracts, idempotent consumers, replay, back-pressure.

  • Hands-on experience building and operating CI/CD pipeline tooling — jobs, shared templates, runners — GitLab CI at fleet scale is a strong plus.

  • Hands-on web application security knowledge: the OWASP Top 10 in real code — able to find these issues, fix them yourself, and encode the detection so they stop recurring.

  • Hands-on experience with SAST, SCA, and secret-scanning tooling (e.g., Semgrep, CodeQL, Snyk, Trivy, Grype, gitleaks), including tuning them to a signal-to-noise ratio developers will tolerate.
  • Demonstrated AI-forward engineering: you actively use AI tooling (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or custom LLM integrations) in your development work today, have opinions grounded in practice about where it helps and where it doesn't, and have built agentic workflows that other engineers adopted.
  • Working knowledge of AWS and Kubernetes as deployment targets for the services you build.

Preferred Knowledge and Skills:

  • Experience in fintech, payments, BNPL, or consumer lending, especially with systems in cardholder-data or regulated scope.
  • Working knowledge of PCI DSS and SOC 2 as they apply to software development and change management — the platform you build is what produces that evidence.
  • Software supply-chain integrity: SBOM pipelines, dependency governance, artifact signing and provenance (Sigstore, SLSA).
  • Familiarity with policy-as-code and admission control (OPA, Kyverno, conftest) — your gates compose with the cluster's runtime policy-enforcement layer.
  • Exposure to bug bounty or external vulnerability report triage — enough to know what the automation you build has to get right.
  • Experience with threat modeling at a system level.

About You:

  • You measure yourself by other teams' code - a fix you shipped is good; a vulnerability class that stopped appearing across the fleet is better.
  • You'd rather ship a gate than publish a policy - you know that enforcement changes behavior and documents do not, and you build the enforcement so well that engineers want to keep it.
  • You have relentlessly high standards - many people may think your standards are unreasonably high. You are continually raising the bar and driving those around you to deliver great results. You make sure that defects do not get sent down the line and that problems are fixed so they stay fixed.
  • You're not bound by convention - your success—and much of the fun—lies in developing new ways to do things.
  • You need action - speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. We value calculated risk-taking.
  • You earn trust - you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully.
  • You have backbone; disagree, then commit - you can respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when doing so is uncomfortable or exhausting.

    You do not compromise for the sake of social cohesion. Once a decision is determined, you commit wholly.

  • You deliver results - you focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, you rise to the occasion and never settle.

Sezzle’s Technology Stack:

  • Languages: Golang, Typescript, Python
  • Frontend: Typescript - React and React Native
  • Backend: Golang
  • Database: MySQL, Postgres, Elasticsearch
  • DevOps & Cloud: AWS, Kubernetes
  • Version Control: Git
  • CI/CD: Gitlab
  • Testing: Developer and AI-driven, focus on automated end-to-end, integration, and unit tests
  • Open Source: Sezzle is focused on using open source, and we build what we can before buying!

What Makes Working at Sezzle Awesome?

At Sezzle, we are more than just brilliant engineers, passionate data enthusiasts, out-of-the-box thinkers, and determined innovators; we are skilled musicians, yogis, cyclists, chefs, golfers, dog-lovers, and rock-climbers. We believe in surrounding ourselves with not only the best and the brightest individuals, but those that are unique and purpose-driven in all that they do. Our culture is not defined by a certain set of perks designed to give the illusion of the traditional startup culture, but rather, it is the visible example living in every employee that we hire.

Bright Vision Technologies is a technology consulting and software development company delivering cloud, AI, data, and enterprise solutions across the United States.

Job Summary
We are seeking an experienced Angular Developer to build modern, enterprise-grade web applications that integrate with Java-based microservices and cloud-native platforms. This role focuses on developing highly responsive Single Page Applications (SPAs) using Angular while collaborating closely with Java backend teams building scalable Spring Boot services. The ideal candidate will possess deep expertise in Angular, TypeScript, and modern front-end development while understanding enterprise application architecture, RESTful services, security, and cloud deployment practices.
You will work alongside Java developers, solution architects, UX designers, DevOps engineers, QA teams, and product owners to deliver scalable, secure, and high-performing enterprise applications supporting financial services, healthcare, retail, insurance, and public sector clients.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, and maintain enterprise-grade Single Page Applications (SPAs) using Angular and TypeScript.

  • Strong debugging, browser profiling, and performance optimization skills using Chrome DevTools and Lighthouse.

Preferred Qualifications

Project Environment
You will be joining an enterprise digital transformation team responsible for modernizing legacy Java applications into cloud-native Angular and Spring Boot platforms. Current initiatives include:

Customer Solutions Engineers are floating technical specialists who partner with CSMs for the duration of a specific need, triggered by things like recurring support cases, asks beyond the typical support experience, or short-term project-based work. The ideal candidate combines deep technical fluency with strong triage judgment and is comfortable moving between engagements without an existing playbook.</p> <h2>What you will do </h2> <ul> <li>Serve as a flexible technical resource CSMs can bring into challenging or recurring account situations that a standard support case isn't built to resolve.</li> <li>Take on short-term, project-based technical engagements for customers without a dedicated TAM.</li> <li>Partner with CSMs to assess customer technical needs, join investigative or best-practices calls, and determine the right next step.</li> <li>Lead hands-on platform optimization: configuration reviews, best-practices setup, and proactive tuning that prevents issues from recurring.</li> <li>Document session recaps and next steps in the CRM so recommendations are clear to the customer and visible to the broader team.</li> <li>Advise customers on underused contracted features and flag upsell or professional services/deployment opportunities where relevant.</li> <li>Recognize when a situation exceeds this role's scope and hand it to the Critical Situation Manager or Technical Support with a clear, documented hand-off.</li> <li>Surface patterns across engagements to Product, Engineering, and Customer Success to drive systemic improvement.</li> </ul> <h2>Must Haves </h2> <ul> <li>3+ years in a customer-facing technical role (email infrastructure, IT security/administration, engineering, or technical support) in enterprise SaaS or cybersecurity</li> <li>Solid grounding in Abnormal's platform and configuration best practices, sufficient to work independently with customers without a senior technical resource in the room</li> <li>Strong triage judgment; data.title: Cloud Network Engineer
data.description:
Cloud Network Engineer – Remote

Bright Vision Technologies is a technology consulting and software development company delivering cloud, AI, data, and enterprise solutions across the United States.
This is a fantastic opportunity to join an established and well-respected organization offering tremendous career growth potential.

Job Title: Cloud Network Engineer
Location: 100% Remote (U.S.)
Position Type: Full-time, Direct W2
Salary Range: $100,000–$150,000 Annually
Experience Required: 10+ years

Sponsorship: U.S. Citizens, Green Card Holders, EAD Holders, and H-1B transfer candidates are encouraged to apply. We are unable to sponsor new H-1B visa petitions for this position.

Job Summary:
We are seeking a Cloud Networking Engineer to design, deploy, and operate cloud networking infrastructure across one or more major cloud providers. The role covers VPC/VNet design, hybrid connectivity, transit topologies, edge networking, DNS, and the security controls that make cloud networking reliable and safe at scale. The ideal candidate combines deep traditional networking knowledge with cloud-native networking patterns, has built production cloud networks at meaningful scale, and brings strong automation discipline to networking work. In this role you will work closely with cross-functional partners — product, design, engineering, operations, and business stakeholders — to translate ambiguous requirements into well-engineered solutions and will be expected to raise the bar through code review, design review, and mentorship of more junior engineers. The successful candidate brings strong engineering discipline, a clear communication style, and a track record of shipping meaningful work that holds up well in production.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and operate cloud networking architectures including VPC/VNet, subnets, routing, and security groups.
  • Build transit hub topologies using AWS Transit Gateway, Azure Virtual WAN, or GCP Network Connectivity Center.
  • Design and implement hybrid connectivity using Direct Connect, ExpressRoute, Cloud Interconnect, and VPN.
  • Architect edge networking including CDN, global load balancing, and WAF integration.
  • Implement DNS strategies including Route 53, Azure DNS, or Cloud DNS with hybrid resolution.
  • Design private connectivity to managed services using PrivateLink, Private Endpoints, or Private Service Connect.
  • Automate cloud networking with Terraform, providing infrastructure-as-code coverage across the network estate.
  • Implement network security controls including firewalls, NACLs, security groups, and DDoS protection.
  • Operate Kubernetes networking including CNI selection, ingress strategies, and service exposure patterns.
  • Build observability for cloud networking including flow logs, traffic insights, and packet capture.
  • Drive cost optimization including data transfer reduction and right-sizing of network resources.
  • Partner with security teams to harden the network perimeter and enforce zero-trust principles.
  • Troubleshoot complex cloud networking issues across cloud and hybrid environments.
  • Stay current with cloud networking platform updates and emerging patterns.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Networking, or a related field.
  • Ten or more years of experience in networking, with significant time on cloud networking.
  • Deep hands-on experience with networking on at least one major cloud provider.
  • Strong understanding of routing, switching, BGP, and modern networking fundamentals.
  • Hands-on experience with hybrid connectivity (Direct Connect, ExpressRoute, or equivalents).
  • Experience with infrastructure-as-code for cloud networking, especially Terraform.
  • Strong understanding of cloud security and network controls.
  • Familiarity with Kubernetes networking and service mesh fundamentals.
  • Strong troubleshooting and packet-level analysis skills.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills.


Preferred Qualifications

  • Cloud networking specialty certifications (AWS Advanced Networking, Azure Network Engineer).
  • Experience with multi-cloud networking and cloud-to-cloud connectivity.
  • Familiarity with SD-WAN platforms and SASE architectures.
  • Experience with eBPF-based networking tools.
  • Exposure to regulated industries with strict network segmentation requirements.


How to Apply

data.title: Senior SRE / DevOps Engineer
data.description:
We are a team of marketing strategists, digital innovators, life science leaders, and other professionals who are driving growth, pushing the envelope, and going above and beyond on behalf of our clients every day.

PharmaForceIQ is a real-time customer engagement platform built specifically for life sciences. We empower leaders across functions and brands with a faster, more effective way to engage healthcare professionals and patients. By streamlining real-time optichannel execution, leveraging AI, and focusing on measurable impact, we are driving a paradigm shift from sluggish, siloed customer engagement efforts to agile, data-driven strategies that deliver unmatched efficiency and tangible results.

Position Overview:

We are seeking a hands-on Senior SRE / DevOps Engineer to design, operate, secure, and continuously improve highly available cloud platforms and delivery systems. The role combines production engineering, cloud operations, Kubernetes platform ownership, CI/CD automation, observability, incident management, and security operations. The successful candidate will own reliability outcomes across application and infrastructure services, reduce operational toil through automation, guide engineering teams on production readiness, and provide expert support for AWS and Amazon EKS. This is a senior individual-contributor role requiring strong technical judgment, disciplined operational practices, and the ability to lead during high-severity incidents.

  • Key Responsibilities:

Source Control & CI/CD Engineering

•Administer Bitbucket and GitLab repos, branching strategies, merge controls, and

release governance.

•Design and maintain Jenkins and GitLab CI/CD pipelines with reusable templates,
shared libraries, and environment promotion models.

•Integrate code-quality, security, container, and secret scanning into pipelines; eliminate
plaintext secrets via approved secret-management platforms.

•Enable safe deployment strategies (rolling, blue-green, canary) with automated
rollback; troubleshoot pipeline, runner, webhook, and dependency failures.

Cloud Operations & AWS Platform Management

•Own cloud environments end-to-end across dev, test, staging, and production: provisioning, patching, backup, recovery, and lifecycle management.

•Operate core AWS services (EC2, Auto Scaling, VPC, ELB, Lambda, Route 53, S3, EBS, IAM, KMS, RDS, EMR, CloudWatch, CloudTrail, Systems Manager) and design resilient multi-AZ network/compute patterns.

•Implement infrastructure as code via Terraform with a peer review, drift detection, and

reusable modules.

•Define and test backup, DR, and HA procedures with documented RTO/RPO; manage tagging, cost optimization, and patching cycles.

Containers, Docker & Amazon EKS

•Lead secure, optimized application Dockerization: multi-stage builds, minimal base images, non-root execution, registry practices.

•Design, provision, upgrade, and support production-grade EKS clusters, managed node groups, networking, ingress, and add-on lifecycle.

•Operate Kubernetes workloads (Deployments, Stateful Sets, Services, Ingress, Jobs, PodDisruptionBudgets) and deploy via Helm and GitOps.

•Implement EKS security controls (RBAC, IAM Roles for Service Accounts, network policies, least privilege); troubleshoot scheduling, networking, and autoscaling issues.

Logging, Monitoring & Observability

•Engineer centralized log management using Splunk and/or Datadog: collection, parsing, retention, dashboards, and alerting.

•Deploy and maintain Prometheus, Grafana, and Alertmanager for platform and application monitoring.

•Define SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, and availability targets; build role-specific dashboards for execs, ops, and engineers.

•Tune alerts to be actionable and severity-based, reducing noise; ensure every critical alert has an owner and runbook.

Reliability & Production Operations

•Participate in and improve the escalation paths.

•Lead major-incident response (triage, stabilization, communication, recovery) and drive blameless post-incident reviews.

•Maintain runbooks, SOPs, dependency maps, and production-readiness checklists; automate repetitive tasks via Python, Bash, and APIs.

•Perform capacity planning, resilience testing, and mentor engineers in troubleshooting and reliability practices.

Security Operations & Vulnerability Management

•Own vulnerability-management workflows across OS, containers, dependencies, cloud, Kubernetes, and CI/CD components.

•Coordinate VAPT: validate findings, assess impact, assign remediation owners, track SLAs, and provide closure evidence.

•Integrate SAST, DAST, dependency, container, IaC, and secret scanning into pipelines; apply hardening baselines.

•Support IAM reviews, key/certificate rotation, privileged-access controls, audit logging, and compliance/risk reporting.

  • Qualifications:
  • 10–12+ years in DevOps, SRE, cloud, platform, or production operations engineering, with 3+ years in a senior/lead capacity.
  • Demonstrated production ownership on AWS: EC2, VPC, load balancers, S3, RDS, EMR, CloudWatch, IAM.
  • Deep hands-on experience with Git, Bitbucket, GitLab, Jenkins, and GitLab CI/CD, including pipeline design, troubleshooting, and governance.
  • Expert-level Docker and Kubernetes experience, including building, operating, and upgrading Amazon EKS clusters and workloads.
  • Hands-on experience with Splunk, and Monitoring with Prometheus, Grafana, and Alert manager.
  • Practical infrastructure-as-code experience (Terraform, Helm) and strong Python/Bash automation skills.
  • Solid understanding of Linux administration, TCP/IP, DNS, TLS, HTTP, load balancing, IAM, storage, and distributed systems.
  • Experience with incident management, RCA, post-incident reviews, SLOs, capacity planning, and backup/recovery.
  • Experience managing vulnerabilities and VAPT findings and implementing security controls across cloud, container, OS, and delivery platforms.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, and calm decision-making under pressure across engineering, security, and business teams.

Why Join Us?

  • Enjoy the flexibility of a fully remote work environment.
  • Competitive base salary (2.5 INR - 3.5 INR). Actual base pay will depend on varying circumstances, including the position, location, individual qualifications, market finances, and other operational business needs.
  • Comprehensive health and wellness benefits package.
  • A collaborative and growing workforce.

Salary: 2.5 INR - 3.5 INR

data.title: Principal ML Platform Engineer
data.description:
Synthesia is the world’s leading AI video platform for business, used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. Founded in 2017, the company is headquartered in London, with offices and teams across Europe and the US.

As AI continues to shape the way we live and work, Synthesia develops products to enhance visual communication and enterprise skill development, helping people work better and stay at the center of successful organizations.

Following our recent Series E funding round, where we raised $200 million, our valuation stands at $4 billion. Our total funding exceeds $530 million from premier investors including Accel, NVentures (Nvidia's VC arm), Kleiner Perkins, GV, and Evantic Capital, alongside the founders and operators of Stripe, Datadog, Miro, and Webflow.

We’re looking for a Principal Engineer to join the ML Platform team at Synthesia.

Our team builds and operates the systems that allow researchers and product teams to train, serve, and deploy generative models reliably and efficiently. This includes research infrastructure, production serving systems, internal tooling, and the platform interfaces that connect them. A growing part of our mission is making these systems more automation-friendly and agent-oriented, so that workflows can increasingly be operated through reliable tooling rather than manual effort.

We’re looking for a strong generalist with a systems mindset:

  • someone who is comfortable working across infrastructure, backend systems, and tooling, and who has seen ML systems in practice.

  • this is not a pure ML Engineer role. We’re especially interested in people who think deeply about reliability, scalability, performance, and resource efficiency in complex production environments.

This is a hands-on IC role with significant ownership. You’ll help shape how our ML platform evolves as we scale the number of models, workloads, tools and teams relying on it.

What you’ll do

  • Design and improve the platform systems that support model training, evaluation, and production serving.

  • Build infrastructure and tooling that make ML workloads more reliable, scalable, and cost-efficient.

  • Develop internal tools and workflows that are easy to operate both by humans and by agents.

  • Work on the architecture behind how models are deployed, served, and operated across research and product environments.

  • Improve how we schedule, monitor, and debug workloads running on GPUs and cloud infrastructure.

  • Develop internal tools and abstractions and agentic systems that reduce operational overhead for researchers and engineers.

  • Drive improvements across observability, automation, reliability, and developer experience.

  • Collaborate closely with researchers and product engineers to understand pain points and turn them into robust platform capabilities.

  • Contribute to technical direction and make pragmatic architectural tradeoffs as the platform grows.

You’ll thrive in this role if you have

  • Strong experience building or operating production systems with a focus on reliability, scalability, and maintainability.

  • A systems mindset: you naturally think in terms of bottlenecks, failure modes, interfaces, resource usage, and long-term operability.

  • Solid hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure, Linux, and infrastructure automation.

  • Experience with Kubernetes and operating distributed workloads in production.

  • Strong coding skills, ideally in Python or similar languages used for backend systems and tooling.

  • Strong judgment around where automation adds leverage, and where human control and reliability matter most.

  • Experience building internal platforms, developer tooling, or infrastructure abstractions used by other engineers.

  • Comfort working in ambiguous environments and taking ownership of open-ended technical problems.

  • A pragmatic approach: you care about solving the right problem well, not over-engineering.

Particularly relevant experience

  • Operating ML infrastructure or model serving systems in production.

  • Supporting research or data-intensive workloads.

  • Working with GPU-based systems or other performance-sensitive infrastructure.

  • Experience with observability and debugging in distributed systems.

  • Familiarity with Terraform, Datadog, GitHub Actions, or similar tools.

Bonus points for

  • Experience building agentic or LLM-powered internal tools.

  • Experience with workflow orchestration systems such as Temporal.

  • Experience working at the boundary between research and production engineering.

  • Familiarity with performance optimization, scheduling, or resource allocation problems.

  • Experience building lightweight product or developer-facing tools.

Apply directly on RemoteJobs.org: https://remotejobs.org/remote-jobs/principal-ml-platform-engineer-synthesia

data.description:
This is a remote position.

Senior System Administrator (IT Infrastructure and Security)Remote (India) | Full-Time Also searched as: Senior Systems Engineer, IT Infrastructure Engineer, L3 Support Engineer, IT Security Engineer

If you were handed admin rights to every system a 425-person company runs on, what would you harden first?

On a typical day you might take an escalation off the systems engineer in the morning and turn its root cause into a runbook they can run next time, walk the MSP through a segmentation change on a Melbourne campus network after lunch, and end the day confirming with the People team that a leaver's access is actually gone.

About Contour

We started in 2020 with a handful of students and a belief that great education should not be out of reach. Today we operate across three brands with 8,000+ students and 425+ team members: roughly 100 in India and 325 onshore in Australia. The India team runs publishing, student experience, CRM and technology, operations, and people and culture.

The people we hire now will shape how Contour grows. This is one of those roles.

About This Role

You are the senior engineer in Contour's first in-house IT team, and the escalation point above it. You run the systems the company works in: Google Workspace, Slack, HubSpot, Rippling and the LMS; the identity platform and the device fleet; the network, CCTV and door access at each campus; and the security posture across all of it.

You report to the interim IT lead in Melbourne until the handover is complete, then to the VP of Global Enablement and Support. They own the technology budget, vendor contracts and the call on which platforms we standardise on. Risk acceptance sits with the senior leadership team. Everything else is yours: the design, the configuration, the hardening, and the no when a vendor does not pass your review.

Expect roughly two thirds of your week on system ownership, hardening and project work, and one third on escalations. The team is you and a systems engineer who runs the L1 and L2 queue. You mentor them and review their work, but this is a hands-on-keyboard seat. Leading the team as it grows is open to you if you want it: welcome, not required.

The standard here is different in two ways. First, you fix the cause. An escalation you close carries a root cause and, if it has come up before, a runbook. Second, you hold the line on security and can explain why. You have said no to something convenient because it was not safe, and you can walk a non-technical executive through that trade-off without dumbing it down or hiding behind acronyms.

Contour has grown to three brands and two countries on systems that were administered alongside other jobs. The interim IT lead has spent the past few months setting the security baseline and documenting it. You take that handover and make it permanent, then build what comes after: identity done properly, a managed fleet, campuses you can see and control from India, and a change process people trust.

By the end of month three, you will have MFA and 2SV at full coverage, a first access review done, and offboarding revocation confirmed rather than assumed. You will have a change record on every production change, the top repeat escalations written into runbooks and handed to the systems engineer, the findings from our recent security review triaged into a dated remediation plan with the first fixes shipped, and the UniFi stack documented for each campus with SPF, DKIM and DMARC enforced on the domain. The controls you put in place in those first months will still be holding when the company is twice this size.

Where the Work Lives

  • Google Workspace:the identity core for staff and where most of the business's data sits. Admin console settings here are security settings: group-driven access, external sharing rules, and audit logs someone reads.
  • Slack:where the company talks and where tickets arrive. Most of what you decide gets explained here, to people who do not administer anything.
  • Rippling and the identity platform:Rippling is the HR system of record, and we are choosing a dedicated identity and device management platform now. Joiner, mover and leaver flows start in Rippling and end with confirmed access, or confirmed revocation, in every system downstream. You inherit the platform decision and run the rollout across a largely BYOD fleet of several hundred macOS and Windows devices.
  • HubSpot and the LMS:the CRM and our own learning platform. Sales, tutors and students work in them, so admin rights, integrations and data flow here protect student data as much as they serve the teams using them.
  • UniFi:the network at each campus, managed from one controller with alerts you cannot ignore. Segmentation, firmware and capacity discipline here are what keep a campus network boring.
  • 1Password:the enterprise password manager. Shared credentials get retired into it, and break-glass accounts are documented, sealed and tested.
  • Suptask:tickets come in through Slack. Each escalation you close records why it happened, so the trend report means something.
  • ​Make.com and Zapier:the automation layer. A scenario that fails silently is worse than the manual step it replaced, so alerting is part of the build.

What You Will Do

  • Take the L2 and L3 escalations and stop them coming back.Close what the systems engineer cannot, record the cause, then write the runbook so that ticket type is theirs from then on.Design identity and access.Role-based access, group-driven permissions, SSO where it is available, MFA and 2SV at full coverage. Run the periodic access review and own the technical side of offboarding.
  • Administer the workplace stack at senior level.The platforms above plus the approved AI platforms, device management across macOS and Windows, and the systems that finance, sales and tutors work in: hardening, admin rights, audit logging, licence use, and the integrations and data flow between them.
  • Run the campus networks, CCTV and door access from India.UniFi design, segmentation, firmware and capacity at each campus; CCTV retention and who can view footage; door access rules and their link to the identity platform. The MSP provides hands on site: you set the scope, run the escalation path, and hold them to their service commitments.
  • Own the security posture end to end.Endpoint security (disk encryption, patch levels, endpoint protection, compliance reporting on the fleet), email and domain security (phishing defence, conditional access, SPF, DKIM and DMARC), credential hygiene through 1Password and break-glass handling, and a security assessment of any new system or vendor before we adopt it. When the answer is no, say no.
  • Lead incident response for security incidents and outages alike.Contain, investigate, keep the timeline, write the RCA with what changed as a result. Close out the findings from our recent security review and keep the remediation on schedule.
  • Put a change record in front of anything touching production.Approver, rollback and verification step, with no exceptions. It exists so the next engineer can see what was done and why.
  • Write it down for whoever inherits it.System references for everything you administer, and guides that make sense to someone who was not there when it was built.
  • Report to the leadership team in plain terms.Ticket trends, availability, licence use and the seats nobody touches; security posture with the cost of fixing something and the cost of leaving it. Bring recommendations with the risk and the alternative you rejected.
  • Build automations that tell you when they break.Make.com or Zapier scenarios with error handling and alerting; the happy path is the easy part. Lead practical AI use across the team: where it helps, where it does not belong, and what it saves.
  • Mentor the systems engineer.Review their tickets, coach the diagnosis, correct habits early. Hiring stays with the IT lead for now.

HubSpot is fixed. Everything else is open: if a better tool exists for something we are doing manually, make the case and we will back it.

Requirements

What You Need

  • Four or more years in systems administration, systems engineering or senior IT support, including at least two years as the accountable administrator for a core business system: the person who decided how it was configured, and the person paged when it broke.
  • Administrator-level Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 at a few hundred users or more. We run Google Workspace, so if your depth is Microsoft 365, show us the concepts carry across.
  • Identity and access as a design discipline: SSO, MFA, an identity provider, and least privilege applied by default.
  • Security you owned, with evidence: hardening, access reviews, patching, endpoint protection, and at least one security incident you handled from detection to write-up.
  • Networking you can diagnose remotely: VLANs, routing, wireless design, and hands-on UniFi or comparable. The campuses are in Australia and you are in India, so working from the controller before you send someone on site is the job.
  • Endpoint management across macOS and Windows at fleet scale, including devices the company does not own.
  • A change process you have followed for real, including at least one change you rolled back cleanly.
  • Scripting to a useful standard: Python, JavaScript or Google Apps Script, and the habit of reading an API reference before asking.
  • Plain English for executives. The leadership team funds what it understands, so a trade-off you cannot explain without acronyms is a fix that does not get approved.
  • ​Comfortable working across the India and Australia time difference; the team you support sits in Melbourne.

Nice to Have

  • Hands-on UniFi, CCTV or door access control work
  • HubSpot, Rippling, Aircall or Notion administration
  • Light scripting or automation: Google Apps Script, Zapier or Make.com scenarios, or basic Python
  • Time in education or another environment that handles student or minor data
  • A diploma, degree or certification in the field: CompTIA A+ or Network+, Microsoft 365 Fundamentals, Google Workspace Administrator

The Kind of People Who​ Thrive Here

The people who do well here see a gap and close it without being asked, holding the bar even when the clock is short. They give a direct read on the work in front of them, including when it's wrong, and when their own idea doesn't hold up, they say so and bring a better one. They build something that keeps running after they step back. Problems here don't show up on schedule or in the same shape twice, and they'd rather make the right call on limited information than let something break while they wait for a sign-off. That's the job. They name the blocker and the ask the moment they have it, on a call or a text, because decisions get made on the information you bring.

Contour's current cluster heads started as team leads. The path from operator to leader is real here.

What good looks like

  • Fast first, then thorough: every ticket gets a quick first response and a fix that holds, in that order.
  • Closed means confirmed: a ticket closes when the person who raised it says it works.
  • Escalations carry evidence: what you tried, what you saw, what you ruled out, so the senior engineer starts where you stopped.
  • Offboarding leaves nothing behind: a leaver's access is gone on the day, with a name against every step.
  • Repeat work shrinks: the queue gets lighter over the year because recurring tickets get automated or documented out of it.

Benefits

Fully remote, anywhere in India. No travel: the campus hardware is in Melbourne and you work it through the MSP and the onshore team. Compensation details shared early in the hiring process. You will hear from us within a week of applying, and the process is a written screen, a short video response, a practical task, and two conversations.

Apply with a CV and one paragraph on a request you slowed down, scoped down or refused because it was not safe, and what happened next.

Apply directly on RemoteJobs.org: https://remotejobs.org/remote-jobs/senior-system-administrator-it-infrastructure-and-security-contour-education

data.description:
Our US Partner is seeking a reliable and detail-oriented E-Commerce Platform Specialist to own the day-to-day operation of their e-commerce platform portfolio. The ideal candidate will manage a proprietary branded store platform built in-house, as well as a third-party enterprise e-commerce platform used for complex client deployments.

This role requires strong technical execution, attention to detail, and the ability to communicate effectively with internal teams, sales departments, and enterprise clients. You will spend most of your time inside the platforms building, configuring, and troubleshooting configurations independently.

This is a full-time role, on a US shift and on a Work From Home set-up.

If you have the right skill set, this may be your opportunity to enter this fast-growing organization.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Platform Operations (70%)

  • Build, configure, and launch branded client stores on both internal and external e-commerce platforms.

  • Handle HTML, CSS, and basic JavaScript customizations independently, without escalating to the development team.

  • Configure products, categories, pricing, access rules, approval workflows, and checkout settings per client.

  • Manage Single Sign-On (SSO) integrations with client identity providers, including Azure AD.

  • Maintain and monitor integrations with warehouse, fulfillment, and ERP systems.

  • Troubleshoot platform issues, isolate root causes, and resolve or escalate them efficiently.

  • Use Git for version control when working on the internal platform codebase.

  • Keep platform records current, including store specifications, configuration decisions, and onboarding runbooks.

Client and Sales Support (20%)

  • Serve as the operational point of contact for active store clients, handling configuration requests, asset updates, and reporting.

  • Work alongside the sales team to scope new store requirements before commitments are made to a client.

  • Translate client briefs into concrete platform configurations, flagging what is native, what needs custom work, and what is out of scope.

  • Support store launches end-to-end, covering requirements gathering, building, QA, and final go-live execution.

Roadmap and Migrations (10%)

  • Feed the internal platform roadmap with client and operational requirements, working closely with the Head of Technology and front-end developers.

  • Plan and execute migrations of existing client stores from legacy platforms like Magento and Shopify onto the current platform stack.

  • Inventory existing store configurations, product catalogs, and integrations before initiating migrations.

  • Manage content and data transfers, re-platforming workflows seamlessly where necessary.

QUALIFICATIONS

Required Experience & Technical Skills

  • 3+ years of hands-on experience operating or building e-commerce stores across multiple platforms.

  • Direct experience with Magento (Open Source or Commerce) and Shopify, including configuration, theming, product setup, and migrations.

  • Proficiency in HTML, CSS, and basic JavaScript with the ability to make layout, styling, and functional changes independently.

  • Comfortable utilizing Git for version control at a basic operational level.

  • Proven experience configuring SSO integrations (Azure AD / SAML 2.0).

  • Deep understanding of e-commerce platform architecture, including routing, templates, product catalogs, variants, and checkout flows.

  • Ability to read and interpret code well enough to debug without always relying on a developer.

  • Conceptual understanding of integrations (APIs, webhooks, and system connectivity) without needing to build them from scratch.

Professional & Behavioral Skills

  • Strong operational instincts with a proactive, can-do attitude—you close loops, document actions, and do not need to be chased.

  • Comfortable working directly and professionally with enterprise clients and sales teams.

  • A "finisher" mindset: able to take a store brief and take it live without constant escalation, spotting platform gaps early.

  • Commercial awareness to know when to push back on requirements that are structurally unfeasible.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and configurations in a fast-paced environment.

Strongly Preferred

  • Experience with company store or branded merchandise platforms (such as Liftoff Commerce, BrightStores, or similar).

  • Familiarity with warehouse or fulfillment integrations (ShipStation, Extensiv, or similar).

  • Exposure to NetSuite or another major ERP in an e-commerce context.

  • Prior experience in the promotional products or branded merchandise industry.
